rationale: bugs_open/040-kafka-dial, instrumentation and structural hygiene ONLY - deliberately no behaviour change on any successful path, because this case's round 1 was vetoed for bundling an unmeasured fleet-wide dial-timeout cut with its instrumentation. Two gaps. (1) The dial counters see a CONNECTION fail; nothing has ever seen a WRITE fail, and writes are failing: MEASURED 2026-08-21 over the retained agent_error_log window, 63 'Kafka write errors' plus 40 'topic partition has no leader' rows across 93 distinct orchestrations, recurring most days since 08-10, mostly at terminal or dispatch steps whose substantive work had already committed. kafka-go never retries the client-side no-leader case - protocol.ErrNoLeader is a bare string type with no Temporary(), so the writer's loop breaks after attempt 1, which is the observed 'Kafka write errors (1/1)' fingerprint. (2) The empty-broker refused bursts RECURRED after the v1.0.1291 getController guard: 94,419 refused over 7 days, 85,887 carrying an empty broker label, which is brokerLabel's output for an address of ':9092'. Since getController can no longer emit that, at least one more producer exists and it is vendored - kafka-go's consumer-group coordinator lookup builds its dial target from an unvalidated FindCoordinator response. Refusing an empty-host dial at the instrumented dialer, under its own label, is the one choke point below vendored code and is the discriminator that settles the mechanism on the next burst.

plan.summary: Add ai_persona_kafka_produce_total{topic_class,outcome} incremented in KafkaProducer.Produce with a bounded outcome vocabulary and a topic normaliser that collapses per-job topics (the cardinality guard), and make instrumentedDialFunc refuse an address with an empty host under a new empty_host outcome. Neither changes any successful path: the produce error text is byte-identical, and an empty-host dial fails with or without the guard - what the guard buys is the label that discriminates a library-internal producer from a repo one. Also wires base/podmonitor.yaml into the kustomize build after 26 days live-but-reconciled-by-nothing, verified as a no-op against the live object.

edits.rationale: classifyProduceErr mirrors classifyDialErr's bounded-label discipline. no_leader is checked first and needs BOTH a typed check and a substring one, because the two no-leader errors behave oppositely: the client-side protocol.ErrNoLeader ('topic partition has no leader') has no Temporary() and is never retried by kafka-go, while the broker-side kafka.LeaderNotAvailable (code 5) IS temporary and has a different text that does not contain 'has no leader'. The composite kafka.WriteErrors that actually arrives embeds member texts without always exposing them to the unwrap chain, which is the same belt-and-braces reason IsMessageTooLarge already carries a substring arm. topicClass is the CARDINALITY GUARD and is not optional: reply topics are minted per job and this cluster has carried ~25,000 topics at once, so a raw topic label on a counter that fires on every produce in the fleet is an unbounded Prometheus series explosion - a worse outage than the one being measured. Every arm returns a fixed string; none returns a substring of its input. The increment sits on both branches and the wrapped error text is UNCHANGED, so every log search and every needle in platform/errors' transient classifier still matches.

Refuse an address whose host is empty before dialling, under its own label, with NO duration observation (nothing was dialled; a ~0s sample would drag the latency distribution this bug is read from). The broker label stays empty so the series is continuous with the 85,887 events already recorded under it. This changes no outcome - a dial to ':9092' goes to the pod's own loopback and fails either way, because net.SplitHostPort(':9092') SUCCEEDS with host='' rather than erroring. What it buys is the discriminator: getController has been structurally unable to emit such an address since v1.0.1291 and the bursts recurred, so a non-zero empty_host post-roll says the remaining producer is library-internal (kafka-go's consumergroup coordinator lookup, which every Reader in the fleet dials through), and this function is the one choke point BELOW vendored code where a guard can be placed at all. THE DISCONFIRMING RESULT IS NAMED: refused with an empty broker label must now be structurally zero, and a non-zero means a third producer exists outside the instrumented dial path.

Pins the outcome vocabulary against the LIVE error shapes verbatim (kafka.WriteErrors wrapping protocol.ErrNoLeader, and our own %w wrapping of it) rather than against constructed ones, and pins the cardinality bound as an ASSERTION rather than a comment: 5,000 distinct per-job topics must yield exactly ONE label value. Mutation C - topicClass returns its input - fails both cardinality tests.
edits.sketch: table test over: WriteErrors{ErrNoLeader}, %w-wrapped ErrNoLeader, bare ErrNoLeader, broker-side LeaderNotAvailable, MessageSizeTooLarge, context.Canceled, DeadlineExceeded, ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET/EPIPE/io.ErrUnexpectedEOF, and an unknown error; plus a net.Error whose Timeout() is true classifying as timeout not network; plus the 5,000-topic bound

edits.rationale: The guard test asserts on the ERROR TEXT, not merely that an error came back: on a machine where something happens to listen on localhost:9090 the dial would otherwise SUCCEED, and only the guard produces that string - so the test discriminates rather than passing by accident. It also asserts the refused counter did NOT move, because separating the two labels is the entire diagnostic value. Two controls: an address SplitHostPort cannot parse must take the ordinary dial path (mutation A, keying on a parse failure, fails both this and the guard test), and a populated host against a real local listener must be untouched. Mutation B, folding empty_host into refused, fails the label-split assertion.

An empty label therefore means the dial's address was :9092' - and section 11.6 records the getController guard proven live on v1.0.1291, which is why a recurrence implicates a different producer.

bugs_open/040 section 6's CORRECTION, which sets this round's scope: the council REJECTED round 1 (hard veto from guardian, 2x HIGH) because it bundled a fleet-wide dial-timeout cut and producer retuning - 'behaviour changes to shared messaging plumbing ... bundled into what was presented as instrumentation ... argued from a remark in this file, NOT from measurement, while building the instrument that would have measured them'. Hence: no retry, no timeout change, and no adapter /metrics extension in this round.
plan.risks: (1) CARDINALITY is the thing that could actually hurt, and it is guarded rather than argued: topicClass returns a fixed string on every arm and a test asserts 5,000 distinct job topics collapse to one label. The rule for future arms is stated at the function and in LANDMINES: no arm may return a substring of its input. The one arm that returns its input (non-agent system.*) is a small fixed set and should be checked by a reviewer. (2) THE EMPTY-HOST GUARD IS THE ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION to 'instrumentation only'. It is defensible because it changes no outcome - the dial fails either way, only the error text, the ~0ms-vs-instant latency and the label differ - and because the address it refuses has a 100% failure rate by construction. If a reviewer disagrees, this edit is SEVERABLE from the counter: they are in different files and neither depends on the other. (3) The guard is placed below vendored code, so it will fire on kafka-go internals we do not control; that is the intent, but it means an unexpected empty-host dial now returns OUR error text rather than the library's, inside library retry loops. It fails identically either way, so no retry policy changes. (4) The counter adds one increment per produce on a hot path; it is a lock-free Prometheus counter with two pre-resolved labels, and classifyProduceErr short-circuits on nil, so the success path costs one map lookup. (5) The PodMonitor wiring changes what a whole-fleet release applies - verified no-op against the live object (only the overlay's environment/region labels are added; spec.selector untouched), and it is the owner's decision, taken this session. (6) WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not close bugs_open/040. The timeout residual is 146 in 7 days and undiagnosed, the node-pinned probe lead is still unexercised, and the refused mechanism is INFERRED, not confirmed - the guard's label is what would confirm it on the next burst.
